text:
oncall-bot: Paging oncall - multiple GPU OOMs during prefill on prod-cluster-7. 4 container restarts in 6m, node flaps seen. Trigger: CUDA OOM in prefill path. Severity: P2. https://redwood.internal/incidents/3267007777
lee: Ack, I'm oncall, joining.
sara: Seeing kube events: pods on node gpu-7b OOMKilled -> CrashLoopBackOff around 01:02Z.
miguel: Runtime logs show `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory` in prefill_worker. Large-context requests (~70k tokens) routed to that node.
ops-tilly: Mit plan: 1) throttle oversized prefill requests, 2) route >X tokens to fallback small-model, 3) reduce prefetch/batch on cluster-7, 4) enable kvcache aggressive trimming for affected runtime group.
lee: Applying quick throttle: add rate-limit for route `/v1/generate` when header `x-prefill-length` > 80000 -> respond 503 + Retry-After.
lee: Running `kubectl -n inference logs runtime-pod-32 --tail=120` and sharing snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T01:02:13Z] prefill: allocate_kv_cache size=4096MB
[2026-03-17T01:02:13Z] prefill: requested 8192MB -> failed
[2026-03-17T01:02:13Z] cuda: out of memory (func=alloc) at /torch/alloc.c:xxx
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/opt/runtime/prefill.py", line 421, in handle_prefill
    kvcache.reserve(requested)
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory
```
miguel: That matches a recent allocator change in runtime image 1.2.9. 1.2.8 had lower steady-state usage.
infra-bot: Initiating rollback: runtime-group-prod -> image runtime:1.2.8 (canary 10% -> will expand if stable). Rolling back now.
sara: Customer impact: two high-volume tenants saw ~5% failed requests and higher tail latency for ~18m. CSM notified.
csm-jordan: Confirmed. Sent initial customer note: "GPU memory pressure caused some request failures; mitigation in progress; we'll follow up with timeline and root cause." :email:
lee: Also reduced prefetch concurrency 4->2 on affected host pool and set `kvcache-evict-on-prefill=true` via configmap patch.
ops-tilly: Suppressed repeat noisy alerts for 30m while stabilizing (not suppressing P1s).
miguel: After rollback to 1.2.8 + throttle rules, restarts dropped to 0 in last 12m. Memory footprint on gpu-7b ~60% lower vs 1.2.9.
oncall-bot: Update: Container restarts: 0 in last 10m. Node flaps cleared. Incident marked mitigated pending postmortem.
lee: Handoff notes for next rotation: collect heap/profile from 1.2.9 vs 1.2.8, run synthetic long-prefill stress tests (70k tokens), add kv-cache growth regression test in CI, and validate allocator guards. Create postmortem ticket and link to incident.
sara: I'll draft the postmortem with customer timeline, mitigation steps, and next actions. Tagging infra for fragmentation vs leak analysis.
csm-jordan: I'll follow up with customers tomorrow with ETA and remediation credits if warranted.
miguel: Opening PR to add per-request kv allocation cap and a feature flag to disable aggressive prefetch for very long contexts.
lee: Rollback completed and routing rules patched. Monitoring for 1h. :white_check_mark: 
ops-tilly: Good work. Postmortem owner: sara; infra lead: miguel. Scheduling review in weekday postmortem meeting.
oncall-bot: Incident status -> mitigated. Summary file: https://redwood.internal/incidents/3267007777/summary
